description: Future-ready manifest for repo-local OpenCode skills. This file does not activate runtime loading by itself; it prepares stable metadata for a future skill registry/loader.

skills.name: artifact-workflow-guard
skills.purpose: Protect artifact-backed workflows from contract drift, truth-mixing, and weakened validation/open boundaries.

responsibilities: persisted artifact loading or lineage validation
validation or preflight for artifact-backed flows
preview, open, review, or replay boundaries
desktop restore or reopen from persisted artifact state

report_requirements: authoritative artifact or handoff boundary after the change
whether validation/preflight and preview/open responsibilities changed
whether legacy compatibility was added, preserved, or rejected
which backend and desktop validation commands passed

skills.name: quant-contract-sync
skills.purpose: Keep backend schemas, route payloads, desktop types, docs, and regression tests synchronized.

responsibilities: contract doc or roadmap wording changes

default: python -m pytest app/tests/test_routes.py app/tests/test_analytics.py app/tests/test_portfolio_allocation_backtests.py app/tests/test_construction_run_service.py app/tests/test_strategy_lab.py app/tests/test_optimizer_service.py

validation_commands: python -m pytest app/tests/test_routes.py app/tests/test_analytics.py app/tests/test_portfolio_allocation_backtests.py app/tests/test_construction_run_service.py app/tests/test_strategy_lab.py app/tests/test_optimizer_service.py
report_requirements: which backend schema and route tests were updated
which desktop types and callers were updated
whether any deprecated fields remain and why

skills.name: portfolio-analytics-guard
skills.purpose: Protect analytics methodology, benchmark separation, schema discipline, and regression coverage.

responsibilities: analytics payload or methodology text changes

default: python -m pytest app/tests/test_analytics.py app/tests/test_importer.py app/tests/test_routes.py app/tests/test_mocked_flows.py

validation_commands: python -m pytest app/tests/test_analytics.py app/tests/test_importer.py app/tests/test_routes.py app/tests/test_mocked_flows.py
report_requirements: what analytics basis changed or remained preserved
whether methodology or assumptions fields changed

questions: Are artifact-workflow-guard and quant-contract-sync still cleanly separated by responsibility?
Is portfolio-analytics-guard staying focused on methodology rather than absorbing unrelated workflow rules?
Do new milestone domains need dedicated skills instead of widening existing ones?

keep_broad_when: the new responsibility matches the skill's primary purpose and invariants
the new responsibility uses substantially the same trigger vocabulary and common trigger paths
the same validation profiles and report requirements still apply
failure modes remain materially the same as the current skill
ownership and review cadence still fit one coherent skill
split_existing_skill_when: one skill starts carrying multiple distinct invariant sets that can drift independently
the same skill would require materially different validation profiles or review workflows
the skill accumulates multiple unrelated failure modes or review owners
maintainers repeatedly need to explain sub-boundaries inside one skill before using it
add_sibling_skill_when: the new domain has a distinct responsibility cluster with its own artifacts, contracts, or regression expectations
the new domain interacts with existing skills but should be linked through recommended_with rather than absorbed
trigger vocabulary and validation surface are distinct enough that maintainers can choose it without ambiguity
roadmap pressure or change velocity shows the domain will continue growing independently
anti_fragmentation_checks: do not split or add a skill if trigger vocabulary, validation profiles, and failure modes are still mostly shared
do not create a new skill just because a new file path appeared
prefer composition through recommended_with before creating a new sibling when the responsibility center is still shared
